bullets.title: Broad tech selloff deepens: semis -8%, AI basket -6.4%, NDX futures -2.8%
bullets.body: Pre-market carnage hits the full AI/semiconductor complex: NVDA -5.3%, AMD -5.8%, MU -6.7%, SNDK -6.8%, DELL -4.9%, HPE -16%, CIEN -6%, VRT -5.6%. SOX is now down 40% off its June peak, giving back Monday's Jensen-bounce entirely. Korean and Japanese chip names (SK Hynix -11%, Samsung -10%) led Asia lower overnight, with NDX futures down ~258bps and E-Mini S&P down ~190bps.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang's return as NVDA CEO restores leadership but doesn't clear fundamental headwinds
bullets.body: NVDA's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, triggering a brief Asian Tech rally, but the bounce faded immediately as California AG Bonta said the reinstatement changes nothing for the criminal probe, BIS restrictions remain contentious, and CoreWeave bonds hit record lows. GS notes the sector needs better rates, credit, and financing conditions plus Q4 AI revenue evidence for a sustained re-rating; JPM argues EPS cut fears from NVDA supply chain should be reduced and sees 20-25% upside for Asian Tech if cuts don't materialize in 2-3 months.

bullets.title: AI bubble thesis gains traction: capital misallocation, circular financing, and credit stress
bullets.body: Multiple bearish narratives converging: George Noble characterizes AI as potentially the greatest capital misallocation in history (shorts IREN and CRWV); a separate note flags token spend leveling off with collapsed pricing and massive contracted compute implying far less AI capex than priced; CoreWeave bonds at record lows highlight circular Nvidia financing concerns; Anthropic token pricing fell 11% in a month. The burden of proof has shifted to AI vendors proving sustainable business models. Hedgeye's #Quad4 framework is YTD +14% long Staples vs -19.8% short Tech.

bullets.title: Section 301 tariffs could arrive today; US prepping broader tariff hikes on EU, China
bullets.body: US is preparing to raise tariffs on dozens of countries including the EU and China (most goods, potentially excluding steel, aluminum, autos), with Section 301 tariff announcements possible as soon as Wednesday. Tariff uncertainty is cited alongside hawkish Fed and AI monetization doubts as three concurrent headwinds compressing risk assets, with particular pressure on tech hardware supply chains and semiconductor names.

bullets.title: Rates/macro backdrop: 10yr at 4.84-4.85%, UST 30yr broke trend support; Quad4 regime
bullets.body: The 10-year yield sits at 4.84-4.85% in pre-market. Hedgeye notes UST 10yr and 30yr broke trend supports at 4.95% and 5.38% respectively — bullish for TLT within their #Quad4 framework. SP500 immediate-term range cited at 6,892-7,316; major averages remain below 50/200-day MAs. Piper notes need a decisive close above SPX 7,350-7,400 to signal a durable low. Core PCE for October expected +0.3% m/m, pushing y/y to +3.4% from +3.1%.

bullets.title: DELL blowout Q3 — $132B AI backlog, FY27 guided to $202B revenue — but stock -5% on margin optics
bullets.body: DELL delivered a monster Q3: EPS $9.45 vs $6.60 consensus, revenue $54.94B vs $49.33B, ISG up ~198% y/y, AI server revenue $22B with backlog at $132.3B after $60.2B in new orders. FY27 guidance raised to $202B revenue and $29.68 EPS. Despite the beat, stock is down 4-7% pre-market due to expected ISG margin step-down in the January quarter and modest AI server sales raise ($74B→$78B). NTM P/E at 9.2x vs 11x 5-year average; $25B buyback authorized.

bullets.title: HPE -16% — worst since 2020 — on Cloud & AI margin guide cut from 18.4% to ~14%
bullets.body: HPE beat Q4 (EPS 83c vs 74c consensus) but guided Q1 EPS midpoint 71c below 72c consensus, and FY27 Cloud & AI operating margins cut from 18.4% to guidance of ~14%, implying Q4 AI networking orders at $1.2bn were the peak. GS TMT notes HPE Financial Services explicitly avoids neocloud/high-risk financing, underscoring the credit squeeze for GPU landlords. Morgan Stanley raises concerns about FY27 earnings sustainability.

bullets.title: WDAY -10%: Q4 subscription guide miss signals third consecutive deceleration
bullets.body: Workday beat F3Q (revenue $2.71B, EPS $2.82, operating margin 31.4%) but guided F4Q subscription revenue to $2.600B — 0.4% below consensus — implying 10% growth vs the prior 12.8%. cRPO expected 10-11% vs Street's 11.5-12%. AI ARR grew 130% y/y to >$750M but monetization remains early. FY28 subscription growth outlook of ~11% and operating margin target of 33%+ offer a floor, but the sequential guide miss triggers the selloff.

bullets.title: APAC data center stress: GPU prices -7%, multiple IPOs delayed, MSFT pulling from deals
bullets.body: GPU pricing in Asia falling ~7% as excess capacity flows to US/European markets. Multiple APAC data center IPOs (DDOC, AIRTRUNK, FIRMUS, NSCL) delayed on development uncertainty and local pushback. FIRMUS seeking $4B in emergency capital after IPO withdrawal. MSFT withdrawing from data center deals in UK and Texas. Banks across APAC are scrutinizing data center operators and AI chip customers for export rule compliance.

bullets.title: AI regulation risk: data center rules could function like a rate hike on economic growth
bullets.body: ROTH warns that AI investments represent 25-33% of US economic growth; tighter data center regulations (export controls, environmental permits, local pushback) could cancel projects and create an economic drag equivalent to a rate hike. Separately, JPM data center power installed base forecast is raised to 303GW by 2028 (38% CAGR), but HVDC adoption lowered to 10-15% on heat constraints and Kyber delay — signaling more nuanced infrastructure buildout than the bull case assumes.

bullets.title: Positioning: HF net selling at extreme levels; US Semis back near long-term average after 6 weeks of selling
bullets.body: JPM prime notes 6 consecutive weeks of hedge fund selling in US Semis; global HF net selling at ~-2z over 20 days, exceeding 2z in North America. Semiconductor short interest rose 10% in early November with largest increases in TXN (+36%), ASML (+34%), AMD (+27%), MRVL (+25%). QQQ short interest at very bearish retail sentiment levels. Retail sold NVDA into Monday's strength. NDX and SOX near TD Combo Buy signals at 12-counts, suggesting potential short-term downside limits.

bullets.title: US consumer resilient: confidence hits 4-month high, Redbook sales +11% y/y, holiday spend survey +12%
bullets.body: PSC Daily Consumer Confidence jumped to 105.4 (up 4.5 pts) on the back of gasoline prices falling 4.1% week-over-week. Weekly Redbook retail sales accelerated to +11% y/y. Citi holiday survey of ~2,500 consumers shows 12% spending growth vs 2025 holiday season ($652 avg), though K-shaped with higher-income cohorts spending +34% while <$25K cohorts spending -3%. 72% remain concerned about food/fuel inflation; online shopping reaching 52% share.

bullets.title: Citi CC data Nov Week 3: total spending -2.2% y/y; Electronics/Jewelry lead, Athletic Footwear -29%
bullets.body: Citi credit card data shows overall spending decelerated slightly in November week 3 to -2.2% y/y (vs -2.0% wk2). Electronics and Cosmetics each grew +6%+ for the 5th and 12th consecutive weeks respectively; Jewelry accelerated to +18.1%. Athletic Footwear continued steep decline at -28.9%. Household Appliances improved 510bps to -3.1%, consistent with the improving BBY results.

bullets.title: Cross-asset signals: Copper -4.4% (3 std devs), USD at Apr 2025 highs, commodities 7% below 200dma
bullets.body: Commodities are flashing stress signals: copper heading toward bear market territory on AI demand doubts and tariff anxiety, down 4.4% overnight (3 standard deviations). BCOM sits ~7% below its 200dma, the widest discount since February 2024. USD is the clearest cross-asset winner with DXY at levels last seen April 2025. WTI down 0.3% to ~$81.42. Japan services PPI printed +4.2% y/y vs +3.6% consensus, fastest since 1990, adding pressure to JGB yields.

bullets.title: SPX 2027 target 8,200 (JPM/MS): 17% EPS growth to $430, re-rate to 19x — but AI rotation risk key swing factor
bullets.body: Both JPM and Morgan Stanley converge on SPX ~8,200 for 2027 based on ~17% EPS growth to ~$430 and re-rating to ~19x. JPM's VIX buy signal last Friday and growth-scare thesis ('unlikely to get fundamental confirmation') supports re-risk over 3-6 months. The key risk: if AI capex slows aggressively (token spend leveling off, efficiency gains, funding pressure), less need for consumer slowdown but meaningful EPS estimate risk in hyperscaler and infrastructure names.

bullets.title: SaaS multiple compression accelerating: IGV -9.5% YTD vs S&P +10.5%; All-SaaS EV/Sales -3.6% w/w
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales vs All-Security at 8.1x; the week-over-week multiple change was -3.57% for SaaS and -7.49% for Security. IGV has returned -9.5% YTD while the S&P 500 is up +10.5%, a 2,000bps gap. WDAY's deceleration print is the latest catalyst for the compression.

bullets.title: Deere F4Q miss and deeply cut FY27 guide signals L-shaped ag recovery extending
bullets.body: DE reported F4Q EPS $3.89 vs $4.05 consensus; FY27 net income guided $4.5-5.25B vs $6.1B consensus — implying EPS of $18-21 vs consensus $22.82. All three equipment segments face margin compression in FY27. Read-through is negative for ag peers CNH and AGCO. Morgan Stanley maintains Overweight but acknowledges results came in below bear case expectations.

bullets.title: Chinese smartphone makers cut 2027 shipment targets 5-29% on high chip costs
bullets.body: Broad-based shipment target cuts across the Chinese smartphone ecosystem for 2027: Xiaomi -25% to 90M units, OPPO -14%, Vivo -29% to 60M, Huawei -16% to below 50M. Apple cutting targets 5.6% to 220M units. Rising DRAM costs and macro uncertainty driving the reductions, adding a demand headwind read-through for memory and mobile chip suppliers.

bullets.title: TSMC Texas: $22.6B campus wins $354M Texas property tax break
bullets.body: Texas approved a $354M property tax abatement for TSMC's planned $22.6B semiconductor manufacturing campus. TSMC was briefly down 9% in Asia overnight on broader sector pressure despite the positive policy signal. The campus approval is a constructive read for US onshoring of leading-edge fab capacity.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: 20% equity drawdown could hit US PCE by 0.3-1.5%; 56% of families own stocks
bullets.body: MS Survey of Consumer Finances shows 56% of US families now own equities (including 59% of middle-income households), with top quintile owning 82% of total equity wealth. A 20% market drawdown translates to 0.3-1.5% of annual PCE depending on wealth consumption propensity — a macro risk amplifier that matters more in a Quad4-type scenario where tech leads the selloff.
